# Rules

66 rules. Severity: `error` is almost always a real defect, `warn` is usually real (read the line), `info` counts toward the slop index and shows in clusters or with `--verbose`.

Change a severity or turn a rule off in `.deslopr.json`; suppress one line with `deslopr-disable-next-line <rule> -- <reason>`.

### prose/chatbot-artifact

**Chat assistant residue** · error · English and French

**Why.** Lines a chat assistant says to its user ended up in the deliverable. Readers notice at once.

**Fix.** Delete the line. A document does not talk about having been written.

Flags:

```markdown
The function returns a list of users. I hope this helps!
```
```markdown
Certainly! Here is the updated README for your project.
```
```markdown
As of my last knowledge update, the API supports three regions.
```
```markdown
Voici une version améliorée de votre texte.
```
```markdown
J'espère que cela vous aide !
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
We hope the new import flow helps teams with large catalogs.
```
```markdown
Here is the configuration file used in production.
```

### prose/chatbot-closer

**Chatbot sign-off** · warn · English and French

**Why.** A generic closing offer adds nothing the reader can act on and is the default ending of assistant replies.

**Fix.** End on the last useful sentence, or give a specific next step (a link, a command, a contact).

Flags:

```markdown
That covers the setup. Let me know if you have any questions!
```
```markdown
Et voilà. N'hésitez pas à me contacter pour la suite.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
Questions go to the #infra channel; the on-call engineer answers within a day.
```

### prose/chat-citation

**Pasted chat citation marker** · error

**Why.** Citation tokens and tracking parameters that chat tools add survive copy and paste and mark the text as pasted.

**Fix.** Remove the marker; if a source matters, cite it as a normal link.

Flags:

```markdown
Revenue grew 12% last year【4†source】.
```
```markdown
See the [docs](https://example.org/guide?utm_source=chatgpt.com).
```
```markdown
The policy changed in March :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
See the [docs](https://example.org/guide?utm_source=newsletter).
```
```markdown
Delete pasted markers such as `【4†source】` before you publish.
```

### prose/placeholder

**Unfilled placeholder** · error · English and French

**Why.** A template slot that never got its value ships as visible filler.

**Fix.** Fill in the real value or remove the sentence.

Flags:

```markdown
Contact us at [Your Email] to get started.
```
```markdown
Signé : [Votre nom]
```
```markdown
<p>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet</p>
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
- [x] Ship the release notes
```
```markdown
Set [the timeout](#timeout) before you deploy.
```

### prose/binary-contrast

**Binary contrast ("it's not X, it's Y")** · warn · English and French

**Why.** Knocking down a claim nobody made to set up the real one is the most recognisable AI cadence.

**Fix.** State Y directly. "The question isn't the model. It's the eval." becomes "The eval matters more than the model."

Flags:

```markdown
It's not a tool, it's a movement.
```
```markdown
This isn't about speed. It's about trust.
```
```markdown
The question isn't the model. It's the eval.
```
```markdown
It is not just a library, but a whole ecosystem.
```
```markdown
Ce n'est pas un outil, c'est une philosophie.
```
```markdown
Il ne s'agit pas de vitesse, mais de confiance.
```
```markdown
Plus qu'un logiciel, une méthode.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
It's not ready for production yet; the migration runs next week.
```
```markdown
It's not common, but if you see it, re-save the series.
```
```markdown
The flag is not required.
```
```markdown
Ce n'est pas grave.
```

### prose/negative-listing

**Negative listing ("No X. No Y. Just Z.")** · warn · English and French

**Why.** Stacking what something is not before saying what it is reads as ad copy written by a template.

**Fix.** Say what it is. Keep one "no" only if the reader actually expected it.

Flags:

```markdown
No fluff. No jargon. Just results.
```
```markdown
No signup, no credit card, just code.
```
```markdown
Pas de blabla. Pas de jargon. Que du concret.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
No. The cache is rebuilt on deploy.
```
```markdown
No tests were run against the staging database.
```

### prose/throat-clearing

**Throat-clearing opener** · warn · English and French

**Why.** An announcement that the point is coming delays the point.

**Fix.** Delete the opener and start with the claim.

Flags:

```markdown
Here's the thing: most dashboards are never opened.
```
```markdown
Let's dive in.
```
```markdown
In this article, we will explore caching.
```
```markdown
In today's fast-paced world, speed matters.
```
```markdown
Soyons honnêtes : personne ne lit la doc.
```
```markdown
À l'ère du numérique, tout va vite.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
The truth table below covers every input.
```
```markdown
We dive into the logs only when an alert fires.
```

### prose/faux-insight

**Faux-insight setup** · warn · English and French

**Why.** "What nobody tells you" casts the writer as the lone expert and promises a secret the sentence rarely delivers.

**Fix.** Cut the setup; let the claim stand on its own evidence.

Flags:

```markdown
Here's what nobody tells you about pricing.
```
```markdown
The part everyone misses: distribution.
```
```markdown
Ce que personne ne vous dit sur le SEO.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
Nobody on the team had used Rust before.
```

### prose/rhetorical-reveal

**Rhetorical setup and reveal** · warn · English and French

**Why.** "The result?" and "What if I told you" stage a reveal instead of stating a fact. It is the cadence of engagement bait.

**Fix.** Write the answer as a plain sentence: "The result? Faster builds." becomes "Builds got faster."

Flags:

```markdown
We cut the bundle in half. The result? A faster app.
```
```markdown
What if I told you tests can write themselves?
```
```markdown
Le résultat ? Une appli plus rapide.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
The result is stored in `out/`.
```
```markdown
What is the result of the second query?
```

### prose/colon-reveal

**Colon reveal** · warn · English and French

**Why.** A noun phrase, a colon, then a lowercase reveal ("The best part: it learns.") is staged drama.

**Fix.** Rewrite as one plain sentence; keep colons for lists, labels and quotes.

Flags:

```markdown
The best part: it learns from every review.
```
```markdown
Le meilleur atout : il apprend tout seul.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
The best part of the release is the new importer.
```
```markdown
Note: run the migration first.
```

### prose/significance-inflation

**Inflated significance** · warn · English and French

**Why.** Calling something pivotal, a testament or a game changer asserts importance instead of showing it.

**Fix.** State the fact and let the reader judge: "marks a pivotal moment" becomes "is the first paid product".

Flags:

```markdown
The launch marks a pivotal moment for the company.
```
```markdown
Caching plays a crucial role in performance.
```
```markdown
Cette fonctionnalité change la donne.
```
```markdown
L'IA joue un rôle essentiel dans notre stratégie.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
The launch is the company's first paid product.
```
```markdown
Caching cut p95 latency from 900 ms to 120 ms.
```

### prose/superficial-analysis

**Trailing "-ing" pseudo-analysis** · warn · English and French

**Why.** A clause like ", highlighting the team's commitment" pretends to explain meaning without adding a fact.

**Fix.** Cut the clause, or replace it with the concrete consequence ("so users can find old drafts").

Flags:

```markdown
The launch adds file search, highlighting the team's commitment to better workflows.
```
```markdown
L'équipe a livré la V2, soulignant ainsi son engagement envers les clients.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
The parser reads the file, ignoring comments.
```
```markdown
Run the linter, then the tests.
```

### prose/weasel-attribution

**Unsourced attribution** · warn · English and French

**Why.** "Experts agree" and "studies show" borrow authority without naming it. The reader cannot check the claim.

**Fix.** Name the source and link it, or drop the claim. Never invent a source.

Flags:

```markdown
Studies show that remote teams ship faster.
```
```markdown
Les experts s'accordent à dire que le SEO est mort.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
Studies show the effect only in teams over 50 people ([Forsgren et al., 2018](https://example.org/accelerate)).
```

### prose/ai-vocabulary

**AI-favored word** · info · English and French

**Why.** Words like delve, tapestry, seamless or leverage are far more frequent in model output than in human writing. One is nothing; a cluster is a tell.

**Fix.** Use the plain word (use, help, strong, smooth) or a concrete fact.

Flags:

```markdown
Let's delve into the details.
```
```markdown
A seamless experience for everyone.
```
```markdown
Un véritable atout pour votre équipe.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
The handler retries twice, then fails.
```

### prose/ai-vocabulary-cluster

**Cluster of AI-favored words** · warn

**Why.** Several different AI-favored words in a short span is one of the strongest signals that text was generated and not edited.

**Fix.** Rewrite the passage in plain words; keep the facts.

**Options.** `{"minDistinct":4,"perThousand":8,"shortText":200,"shortMinDistinct":3}`

Flags:

```markdown
Our robust platform seamlessly empowers teams to leverage cutting-edge insights.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
Our platform syncs your calendar every five minutes and flags double bookings.
```

### prose/filler-phrase

**Filler phrase** · info · English and French

**Why.** Phrases like "it's worth noting that" delay the point and pad the rhythm.

**Fix.** Delete the phrase; the sentence usually works without it.

Flags:

```markdown
It's worth noting that the API is rate limited.
```
```markdown
Il est important de noter que le cache expire.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
The API allows 100 requests per minute.
```

### prose/summary-ending

**Recap ending** · warn · English and French

**Why.** "In conclusion" and a closing paragraph that restates the piece repeat what the reader just read.

**Fix.** End on the last concrete point, decision or next step.

Flags:

```markdown
We moved the queue to Redis.

In conclusion, the new setup is faster and simpler.
```
```markdown
Le cache est réparé.

En conclusion, tout fonctionne mieux.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
The conclusion of the audit is in `audit.md`.
```

### prose/hedge-stack

**Stacked hedges** · warn · English and French

**Why.** Two hedges on one claim ("could potentially") say the writer is not committing to anything.

**Fix.** Keep one hedge if the uncertainty is real, or state the claim.

Flags:

```markdown
This change could potentially break older clients.
```
```markdown
Cette option pourrait potentiellement ralentir le site.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
This change breaks clients older than 2.3.
```

### prose/false-range

**False range ("whether you're a X or a Y")** · warn · English and French

**Why.** Addressing every possible reader at once addresses none of them.

**Fix.** Name the reader this is for, or cut the sentence.

Flags:

```markdown
Whether you're a solo founder or a Fortune 500 team, we've got you covered.
```
```markdown
Que vous soyez freelance ou grand groupe, cet outil est fait pour vous.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
Whether the job retries depends on the exit code.
```

### prose/mic-drop

**Mic-drop line** · warn · English and French

**Why.** "That's it. That's the whole trick." and "Let that sink in" perform profundity instead of making a point.

**Fix.** Delete the line and end on the clearest concrete sentence already there.

Flags:

```markdown
Ship small. That's it. That's the whole strategy.
```
```markdown
Tests matter. Period.
```
```markdown
Le code est une dette. Point final.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
That's it for setup; the next section covers deploys.
```
```markdown
The billing period ends on the 30th.
```

### prose/em-dash-density

**Em dash saturation** · warn

**Why.** Humans use em dashes, but models use them as a rhythm crutch. Many of them in little text is a strong tell.

**Fix.** Replace most with commas, colons, parentheses or two sentences. One or two in a long piece is fine.

**Options.** `{"min":3,"perThousand":5,"shortText":150,"shortMin":2}`

Flags:

```markdown
Fast — secure — and built for teams. It ships today — and it is free.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
The build takes four minutes. Most of that is the type check, which we cache.
```
```markdown
— Bonjour, dit-elle.
— Bonjour.
```

### prose/emoji-decoration

**Emoji as decoration** · warn

**Why.** Emoji in headings and emoji bullet lists are the default formatting of generated posts and READMEs.

**Fix.** Remove them; let headings and list items carry their own words.

Flags:

```markdown
## 🚀 Getting started

Install it.
```
```markdown
- ✅ Fast
- ✅ Secure
- ✅ Simple
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
## Getting started

Install it with npm.
```
```markdown
Copyright © 2026 Example
```

### prose/bold-overuse

**Bold everywhere** · info

**Why.** Bold sprinkled through sentences, or a list of "**Label:** text" items, is generated-document formatting. When everything is emphasised, nothing is.

**Fix.** Keep bold for the one thing a skimming reader must not miss; turn label lists into prose or a table.

Flags:

```markdown
- **Speed:** fast
- **Security:** strong
- **Scale:** big
- **Support:** 24/7
- **Price:** low
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
Run **one** migration at a time.
```

### code/elided-code

**Placeholder standing in for code** · error

**Why.** "// ... rest of the code" or "# existing implementation here" means an agent replaced real code with a placeholder. Whatever was there is gone.

**Fix.** Restore the missing code from git history, or write it. Never ship the placeholder.

Flags:

```js
function save(user) {
  // ... rest of the code
}
```
```py
class Cart:
    # existing methods remain unchanged
    pass
```

Does not flag:

```js
// Keep the rest of the queue untouched when one job fails.
run();
```

### code/edit-narration

**Comment narrates the edit** · warn

**Why.** "// Added error handling" or "// Now uses the new API" describes the diff, not the code. It is true for one commit and noise forever after.

**Fix.** Delete it, or rewrite it to say why the code is this way. History belongs in the commit message.

Flags:

```ts
// Added error handling for the fetch call
const res = await fetch(url);
```
```py
# Now uses the new pricing API
price = get_price(sku)
```
```go
// FIX: changed timeout to 30s
const timeout = 30
```

Does not flag:

```ts
// Retries cover the 502s the gateway returns during deploys.
const res = await fetchWithRetry(url);
```
```py
# Removed items stay in the trash for 30 days.
purge(items)
```
```js
// Added code is compared against the base branch.
// changed: repo-relative paths of edited files.
scan(changed);
```

### code/review-provenance

**Review history in a code comment** · warn

**Why.** "Per the reviewer's request" or "addressed feedback" records how the code was negotiated, not what it does.

**Fix.** Say why the code is this way, or delete the comment. Put review history in the PR.

Flags:

```js
// Per the reviewer, use a Map here
const seen = new Map();
```

Does not flag:

```js
// A Map keeps insertion order, which the report relies on.
const seen = new Map();
```

### code/narrating-comment

**Comment restates the next line** · info

**Why.** "// Initialize the counter" above "let counter = 0" doubles the reading without adding anything. Three or more in one file is a strong tell.

**Fix.** Delete it. A comment earns its line by saying what the code cannot: a reason, a constraint, a trap.

**Options.** `{"clusterAt":3}`

Flags:

```js
// Initialize the counter
let counter = 0;
```
```py
# Return the result
return result
```

Does not flag:

```js
// Start at 1: row 0 is the header.
let counter = 1;
```

### code/step-comments

**Step-by-step narration** · warn

**Why.** "// Step 1: validate input", "// Step 2: ..." numbers what the control flow already shows.

**Fix.** Delete the step labels. If the flow is hard to follow, split it into named functions.

Flags:

```ts
// Step 1: Validate input
validate(x);
// Step 2: Process
process(x);
// Step 3: Return
return x;
```

Does not flag:

```ts
// Step 1 of the OAuth dance happens in the browser, see login.ts.
exchange(code);
```

### code/banner-comment

**Decorative banner comment** · info

**Why.** A label boxed between rows of ===== or ───── is decoration. The block itself is a classic generated-code signature.

**Fix.** Use one plain comment line, or none; if a file needs sections, it may need splitting.

Flags:

```py
# ==========================================
# CONFIGURATION
# ==========================================
DEBUG = False
```

Does not flag:

```py
# Configuration is read once at import time.
DEBUG = False
```

### code/emoji-in-code

**Emoji in comments or log lines** · warn

**Why.** ✅, 🚀 and 🔥 in comments and log output are the default vocabulary of generated code, and they break grep and some terminals.

**Fix.** Write the word ("done", "failed") or nothing.

Flags:

```js
console.log("✅ Server started");
```
```py
# 🚀 Fast path
run()
```

Does not flag:

```js
console.log("Server started on", port);
// © 2026 Example Inc.
```

### code/swallowed-error

**Error swallowed silently** · warn

**Why.** An empty catch or "except Exception: pass" turns a visible crash into invisible corruption. Agents add them to make errors go away.

**Fix.** Catch the specific error you expect and handle it, or let it raise. If ignoring is deliberate, say why in a comment inside the block.

Flags:

```py
try:
    sync()
except Exception:
    pass
```
```ts
try {
  sync();
} catch (e) {}
```
```js
load().catch(() => {});
```

Does not flag:

```py
try:
    n = int(s)
except ValueError:
    n = 0
```
```ts
try {
  fs.unlinkSync(tmp);
} catch {
  // The file may already be gone; nothing to clean.
}
```

### code/speculative-generality

**Code kept "for future use"** · warn

**Why.** Flexibility for a future nobody asked for costs review, grep hits and false confidence today.

**Fix.** Delete what has no caller (git remembers). Add the abstraction when the second use case arrives.

Flags:

```ts
// Kept for future use
export function toXml(r) { return ""; }
```

Does not flag:

```ts
// Used by the nightly export job (jobs/export.ts).
export function toXml(r) { return ""; }
```

### code/vague-todo

**TODO with no task in it** · info

**Why.** "TODO: improve this" names a feeling, not a task. Nobody can act on it.

**Fix.** Write what, and why, or delete it.

Flags:

```js
function f() {
  // TODO: improve this
}
```

Does not flag:

```js
// TODO(#412): stream rows instead of loading the whole CSV once files pass 1 GB.
```

### code/redundant-docstring

**Docstring echoes the signature** · warn

**Why.** """Get the user.""" on get_user(), or "@param name The name.", says nothing the signature does not.

**Fix.** Delete it, or document what the name cannot say: units, edge cases, errors, side effects.

Flags:

```py
def get_user(user_id):
    """Get the user."""
    return db[user_id]
```
```ts
/** Gets the user. */
export function getUser(id: string) {}
```
```js
/**
 * @param {string} name The name.
 */
function greet(name) {}
```

Does not flag:

```py
def get_user(user_id):
    """Raises KeyError for deleted users; callers show a 404."""
    return db[user_id]
```

### code/debugger-left

**Debugger statement left in** · error

**Why.** A breakpoint in committed code stops or slows every run that hits it.

**Fix.** Remove it.

Flags:

```js
function f(x) {
  debugger;
  return x;
}
```
```py
def f(x):
    breakpoint()
    return x
```

Does not flag:

```js
// Set a breakpoint here with `debugger` when tracing.
function f(x) { return x; }
```

### code/test-cannot-fail

**Test that cannot fail** · warn

**Why.** A test with no assertion, or one that asserts a constant, passes whatever the code does. It inflates coverage and hides regressions.

**Fix.** Assert on behavior the user would notice, including a failure case.

Flags:

```js
test('adds item', () => {
  const cart = new Cart();
  cart.add('apple');
});
```
```py
def test_add():
    cart = Cart()
    cart.add("apple")
```
```ts
it('works', () => {
  expect(true).toBe(true);
});
```

Does not flag:

```js
test('adds item', () => {
  const cart = new Cart();
  cart.add('apple');
  expect(cart.count).toBe(1);
});
```
```py
def test_add():
    cart = Cart()
    cart.add("apple")
    assert cart.count == 1
```

### code/version-suffix

**_v2 / _new / _fixed clone** · info

**Why.** An agent that does not dare change foo writes foo_v2 next to it. Now there are two sources of truth and future fixes land in one.

**Fix.** Merge them into one name. Keep a suffix only during a documented migration.

Flags:

```py
def parse(s):
    return s

def parse_v2(s):
    return s.strip()
```
```ts
function renderChartFixed(data) { return data; }
```

Does not flag:

```ts
function isNew(user) { return true; }
const vec2 = (x, y) => [x, y];
function getUsersV2() {}
```

### code/commented-out-code

**Block of commented-out code** · info

**Why.** Old versions left in comments are the debris of an attempt that was replaced. Git already keeps them.

**Fix.** Delete the block.

Flags:

```js
// const old = load();
// if (old) {
//   save(old);
// }
run();
```

Does not flag:

```js
// Load once at startup; the cache
// is invalidated by the watcher.
run();
```

### code/fallback-import

**Try-import fallback** · info

**Why.** try: import fast_x / except ImportError: import x gives two code paths and usually tests one.

**Fix.** Declare the dependency, or make it a real optional extra with a test for the fallback.

Flags:

```py
try:
    import ujson as json
except ImportError:
    import json
```

Does not flag:

```py
import json
```

## Interfaces

| Rule | Severity | What it catches |
|---|---|---|
| [`ui/ai-gradient`](#uiai-gradient) | warn | Purple-blue default gradient |
| [`ui/gradient-text`](#uigradient-text) | warn | Gradient text |
| [`ui/glow-shadow`](#uiglow-shadow) | warn | Colored glow |
| [`ui/blurred-orb`](#uiblurred-orb) | warn | Decorative blurred color orb |
| [`ui/side-stripe`](#uiside-stripe) | warn | Colored side stripe on cards |
| [`ui/glass-stack`](#uiglass-stack) | warn | Glassmorphism on everything |
| [`ui/eyebrow-label`](#uieyebrow-label) | warn | Eyebrow label or pill above the headline |
| [`ui/unsourced-stat`](#uiunsourced-stat) | warn | Statistic with no source |
| [`ui/unverified-claim`](#uiunverified-claim) | warn | Compliance or security claim to verify |
| [`ui/placeholder-person`](#uiplaceholder-person) | warn | Placeholder or random person |
| [`ui/dead-control`](#uidead-control) | warn | Control that does nothing |
| [`ui/emoji-icon`](#uiemoji-icon) | warn | Emoji used as an icon |
| [`ui/missing-alt`](#uimissing-alt) | warn | Image without alt text |
| [`ui/focus-removed`](#uifocus-removed) | warn | Focus outline removed with no replacement |
| [`ui/clickable-div`](#uiclickable-div) | warn | Click handler on a div |
| [`ui/overused-font`](#uioverused-font) | info | Default AI typeface |
| [`ui/generic-ai-icon`](#uigeneric-ai-icon) | info | Sparkle, wand and rocket icons |
| [`ui/generic-cta`](#uigeneric-cta) | info | Generic call to action |
| [`ui/bounce-easing`](#uibounce-easing) | info | Bounce and elastic motion |
| [`ui/fake-window-chrome`](#uifake-window-chrome) | info | Fake terminal or window chrome |
| [`ui/pulsing-dot`](#uipulsing-dot) | info | Decorative pulsing dot |

### ui/ai-gradient

**Purple-blue default gradient** · warn

**Why.** Purple-to-blue, violet-to-pink and indigo-to-cyan gradients are the most recognisable color tell of generated interfaces.

**Fix.** Pick color from the product's own identity. If a gradient stays, write down what it serves.

Flags:

```tsx
<div className="bg-gradient-to-r from-purple-600 to-blue-500 p-8">Hi</div>
```
```css
.hero { background: linear-gradient(135deg, #7c3aed 0%, #3b82f6 100%); }
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
<div className="bg-gradient-to-b from-amber-100 to-orange-200">Hi</div>
```
```css
.fade { background: linear-gradient(to bottom, #fff, #f4f4f5); }
```

### ui/gradient-text

**Gradient text** · warn

**Why.** Gradient-filled headings and metrics are decoration standing in for hierarchy, and they often fail contrast.

**Fix.** Use a solid color; get emphasis from size and weight.

Flags:

```jsx
<h1 className="bg-gradient-to-r from-pink-500 to-violet-500 bg-clip-text text-transparent">Build</h1>
```

Does not flag:

```jsx
<h1 className="text-4xl font-bold text-zinc-900">Build</h1>
```

### ui/glow-shadow

**Colored glow** · warn

**Why.** A zero-offset colored halo on cards, buttons and icons is decoration, not depth. Glow everywhere is a generated-UI signature.

**Fix.** Use offset, soft, neutral shadows for elevation, or none.

Flags:

```tsx
<button className="rounded-xl shadow-lg shadow-purple-500/50">Go</button>
```
```css
.card { box-shadow: 0 0 40px rgba(139, 92, 246, 0.6); }
```

Does not flag:

```css
.card { box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12); }
```

### ui/blurred-orb

**Decorative blurred color orb** · warn

**Why.** An absolutely positioned, heavily blurred purple or blue circle behind the hero is the default "ambient" background of generated landing pages.

**Fix.** Remove it, or replace it with imagery or texture that comes from the product.

Flags:

```tsx
<div className="absolute -top-20 h-96 w-96 rounded-full bg-purple-500/30 blur-3xl" />
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
<img className="h-12 w-12 rounded-full" src="/team/ana.jpg" alt="Ana Ruiz" />
```

### ui/side-stripe

**Colored side stripe on cards** · warn

**Why.** A thick colored border on one side of a rounded card or callout is one of the most recognisable tells of generated UI.

**Fix.** Drop the stripe; mark state with an icon, a label or the background.

Flags:

```tsx
<div className="rounded-lg border-l-4 border-indigo-500 bg-white p-4">Tip</div>
```
```css
.callout { border-left: 4px solid #6366f1; border-radius: 8px; }
```

Does not flag:

```css
blockquote { border-left: 4px solid #ccc; padding-left: 1rem; }
```

### ui/glass-stack

**Glassmorphism on everything** · warn

**Why.** Backdrop blur on the navbar, the cards, the modal and the sidebar at once is trend stacking with no hierarchy left.

**Fix.** Keep blur for the one surface that floats over content, or none.

**Options.** `{"max":2}`

Flags:

```tsx
<nav className="backdrop-blur-md" />
<div className="backdrop-blur-lg" />
<aside className="backdrop-blur" />
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
<nav className="backdrop-blur-md" />
```

### ui/eyebrow-label

**Eyebrow label or pill above the headline** · warn

**Why.** A tiny uppercase, letter-spaced label (or a small pill chip) parked right above the H1 is the default hero of generated pages, and it usually repeats what the heading says.

**Fix.** Delete it and let the heading carry the page.

Flags:

```tsx
<section>
  <p className="text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-widest text-indigo-500">AI-powered analytics</p>
  <h1 className="text-5xl">Understand your data</h1>
</section>
```
```vue
<template>
  <span class="rounded-full border px-3 py-1 text-xs">New in 2.0</span>
  <h1>Ship faster</h1>
</template>
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
<section>
  <h1 className="text-5xl">Understand your data</h1>
  <p className="text-lg">Connect a warehouse and ask questions in SQL.</p>
</section>
```

### ui/unsourced-stat

**Statistic with no source** · warn

**Why.** "10K+ users", "99.9% uptime" and "3x faster" are the numbers generators invent to fill a hero. Unverified, they are fabrication.

**Fix.** Use a real, sourced number, or remove it. Never invent metrics, logos or testimonials.

Flags:

```tsx
<p className="text-sm">Trusted by 10,000+ teams worldwide</p>
```
```html
<span>99.9% uptime</span>
```
```tsx
const stats = [{ label: "Join 50K+ developers shipping faster" }];
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
<p>Used by 312 teams (<a href="/customers">see the list</a>)</p>
```
```markdown
The migration takes about a minute for 1,000 users and is safe to re-run.
```

### ui/unverified-claim

**Compliance or security claim to verify** · warn

**Why.** "SOC 2 compliant" and "bank-grade encryption" are claims generators add to look credible. False, they are a legal problem, not a style one.

**Fix.** Keep the claim only if it is true and documented; link the evidence.

Flags:

```tsx
<li>SOC 2 Type II compliant</li>
<li>Bank-grade encryption</li>
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
<li>Data stored in Frankfurt (eu-central-1)</li>
```

### ui/placeholder-person

**Placeholder or random person** · warn

**Why.** Random avatar services and "Jane Doe, CEO" make testimonials and team sections that are fabricated by construction.

**Fix.** Use real people with their consent, or an honest empty state. Never fake a testimonial.

Flags:

```tsx
<img src="https://i.pravatar.cc/150?img=3" alt="" />
<p>Jane Doe, CEO at TechCorp</p>
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
<img src="/team/ana.jpg" alt="Ana Ruiz" />
```

### ui/dead-control

**Control that does nothing** · warn

**Why.** href="#", empty onClick handlers and links to nowhere look finished in a screenshot and fail the first click.

**Fix.** Wire it to a real destination or action, or remove it. If it is pending, label it visibly.

Flags:

```tsx
<a href="#">Pricing</a>
<button onClick={() => {}}>Buy</button>
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
<a href="#pricing">Pricing</a>
<button onClick={() => checkout(plan)}>Buy</button>
```

### ui/emoji-icon

**Emoji used as an icon** · warn

**Why.** Emoji standing in for an icon system (🚀 on every feature card) renders differently on every platform and reads as filler.

**Fix.** Use one consistent icon set, or no icon.

Flags:

```tsx
const features = [{ icon: "🚀", title: "Fast" }];
<h3>⚡ Lightning fast</h3>
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
<h3><BoltIcon aria-hidden /> Fast builds</h3>
```

### ui/missing-alt

**Image without alt text** · warn

**Why.** Screen readers announce the file name or nothing. Generated markup often drops alt.

**Fix.** Describe the image in alt, or use alt="" if it is purely decorative.

Flags:

```html
<img src="/hero.png" class="w-full">
```

Does not flag:

```html
<img src="/hero.png" alt="Dashboard showing weekly revenue">
<img src="/dots.svg" alt="">
```

### ui/focus-removed

**Focus outline removed with no replacement** · warn

**Why.** outline: none without a visible focus style makes the interface unusable from the keyboard.

**Fix.** Keep the outline, or replace it with a :focus-visible style (ring, border, offset).

Flags:

```css
button { outline: none; }
```
```tsx
<input className="outline-none border px-2" />
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
<input className="outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-blue-600" />
```

### ui/clickable-div

**Click handler on a div** · warn

**Why.** A div with onClick is not focusable and not announced as a control.

**Fix.** Use a <button> (or <a> for navigation).

Flags:

```tsx
<div className="card" onClick={() => open(id)}>Open</div>
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
<button type="button" className="card" onClick={() => open(id)}>Open</button>
```

### ui/overused-font

**Default AI typeface** · info

**Why.** Inter, Roboto, Poppins, Plus Jakarta Sans, Space Grotesk and Geist are what generators reach for with no brief. Fine with a reason; a tell without one.

**Fix.** Choose the face for the brand's character, and write the reason down. Allow your brand font in config.

**Options.** `{"fonts":["Inter","Roboto","Poppins","Montserrat","Open Sans","Plus Jakarta Sans","Space Grotesk","Geist","DM Sans","Outfit","Manrope","Lato","Fraunces"],"allow":[]}`

Flags:

```css
body { font-family: "Inter", sans-serif; }
```
```tsx
import { Inter } from 'next/font/google';
```

Does not flag:

```css
body { font-family: "Söhne", system-ui, sans-serif; }
```

### ui/generic-ai-icon

**Sparkle, wand and rocket icons** · info

**Why.** Sparkles, magic wands, bolts, rockets and robot heads signal "AI" by reflex and say nothing about the feature.

**Fix.** Pick an icon that depicts what the feature does, or none.

Flags:

```tsx
import { Sparkles, Zap, Rocket, Shield } from 'lucide-react';
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
import { Calendar, Mail } from 'lucide-react';
```

### ui/generic-cta

**Generic call to action** · info

**Why.** "Get Started", "Learn More" and "Explore" name no action. The button should say what happens next.

**Fix.** Name the action: "Create a workspace", "Read the API docs", "Book a demo".

Flags:

```tsx
<button className="btn">Get Started →</button>
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
<button className="btn">Create a workspace</button>
```

### ui/bounce-easing

**Bounce and elastic motion** · info

**Why.** Bouncing and elastic easing feels dated and draws the eye for no reason.

**Fix.** Use a smooth ease-out; reserve motion for one authored moment.

Flags:

```tsx
<div className="animate-bounce">↓</div>
```

Does not flag:

```css
.in { transition: transform 200ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); }
```

### ui/fake-window-chrome

**Fake terminal or window chrome** · info

**Why.** Three red-yellow-green dots on a dark box, typing out commands, is the stock "developer tool" hero visual.

**Fix.** Show the real product, or a real screenshot.

Flags:

```tsx
<div className="flex gap-2"><span className="h-3 w-3 rounded-full bg-red-500" /><span className="h-3 w-3 rounded-full bg-yellow-500" /><span className="h-3 w-3 rounded-full bg-green-500" /></div>
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
<span className="bg-green-500">Online</span>
```

### ui/pulsing-dot

**Decorative pulsing dot** · info

**Why.** A small pinging dot simulates liveness. Unless it reflects live data, it is decoration that pulls attention.

**Fix.** Use a static indicator, or tie the animation to real state.

Flags:

```tsx
<span className="h-2 w-2 rounded-full bg-green-500 animate-ping" />
```

Does not flag:

```tsx
<div className="h-24 animate-pulse rounded bg-zinc-100" aria-busy="true" />
```

## Repository hygiene

| Rule | Severity | What it catches |
|---|---|---|
| [`repo/secret`](#reposecret) | error | Committed credential |
| [`repo/merge-conflict`](#repomerge-conflict) | error | Conflict markers committed |
| [`repo/local-path`](#repolocal-path) | warn | Machine-local path |
| [`repo/invisible-unicode`](#repoinvisible-unicode) | warn | Invisible or bidirectional characters |
| [`repo/agent-report-file`](#repoagent-report-file) | warn | Agent report committed as a file |
| [`repo/duplicate-file`](#repoduplicate-file) | warn | Second copy of a file |

### repo/secret

**Committed credential** · error

**Why.** Agents paste working keys into config and examples to make things run. A pushed key is a leaked key.

**Fix.** Remove it, rotate it, and read it from the environment or a secret store.

Flags:

```js
const key = "ghp_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789";
```

Does not flag:

```js
const key = process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN;
```

### repo/merge-conflict

**Conflict markers committed** · error

**Why.** A half-resolved merge breaks the file and usually the build.

**Fix.** Resolve the conflict and remove the markers.

Flags:

```js
<<<<<<< HEAD
const a = 1;
=======
const a = 2;
>>>>>>> main
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
Title
=======

Text.
```

### repo/local-path

**Machine-local path** · warn

**Why.** An absolute path into someone's home folder works on one laptop and nowhere else.

**Fix.** Use a path relative to the project, an environment variable, or a placeholder.

Flags:

```sh
cp dist/* /Users/kevin/projects/site/
```
```json
{ "out": "C:\\Users\\marc\\Desktop\\out" }
```

Does not flag:

```sh
cp dist/* "$HOME/site/"
# e.g. /Users/you/site
```
```markdown
Skills live in C:\Users\You\.claude\skills on Windows.
```
```markdown
Vos fichiers sont dans /Users/vous/projets/site.
```

### repo/invisible-unicode

**Invisible or bidirectional characters** · warn

**Why.** Zero-width spaces ride along when text is pasted from a chat window; bidi controls in code can hide what it really does.

**Fix.** Delete them. In code, a bidi control should never be there.

Flags:

```markdown
The build​ passes on main.
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
The build passes on main.
```

### repo/agent-report-file

**Agent report committed as a file** · warn

**Why.** IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md, FIXES_APPLIED.md and friends are an agent's notes to its user. They go stale the moment they land.

**Fix.** Move what matters into the PR description, the changelog or real docs, and delete the file.

Flags:

```markdown
# Summary
```
```markdown
# Fixes
```

Does not flag:

```markdown
# Summary
```
```markdown
# Bug
```
```markdown
# Changelog
```

### repo/duplicate-file

**Second copy of a file** · warn

**Why.** utils_v2.py, Header.old.tsx and "config copy.json" are forks of one file. Fixes now land in one copy.

**Fix.** Keep one file. History lives in git.

Flags:

```py
x = 1
```
```tsx
export {};
```

Does not flag:

```py
x = 1
```
```sql
select 1;
```
